title: Barb Howard
wikitext:
{{Infobox character |games =FOTV |name =Barb Howard |image =FOTV Barb.png |race =[[Human]] |gender =Female |family =[[The Ghoul|Cooper Howard]] - ex-husband
[[Janey Howard]] - daughter |affiliation =[[Vault-Tec Corporation]] |role =Vault-Tec executive |status = |TV actor =[[Frances Turner]] }} {{Quotation|Every day I go into work, and I think about how humanity can survive a nuclear event that WILL wipe out 90% of life on Earth, and I come home, and you're talking to me about hiding out in a ranch up in Bakersfield! You know, I don't even know what planet you're on sometimes, Coop.|Barb to her husband|sound=Barb Howard.ogg}} '''Barbara "Barb" Howard'''{{FOTV|2|3}}, seen on side of Barb's suitcase around ~13:00 is the mother of [[Janey Howard]] and the ex-wife of [[The Ghoul|Cooper Howard]] who was employed as a high-ranking executive of the [[Vault-Tec Corporation]] before the [[Great War]]. ==Background== {{Quotation|Barb works in a high-ranking position for the Vault-Tec Corporation. She and Cooper Howard have a daughter together, Janey, and Barb has focused on advancing her position in Vault-Tec to ensure her family's place in a "good vault."|[[Fallout season 2 Amazon overview|''Fallout'' season 2 character description]]}} It is unknown where and when Barb met Cooper, but he claims to have fallen in love with her because of her resolve to always try to do what she believes is right. Cooper proposed to Barb during a vacation to [[Catalina]], after going to what he described as a "romantic point" along the rocks which he remembers as being "covered in seagull shit." Nonetheless, it was a success, as Barb accepted his proposal and eventually married him.[[The Ghoul|Cooper Howard]]: ''"Last night I was thinking about when I proposed to you. Catalina. We walked out to that... romantic point. "''
Barb Howard: ''"'''*chuckles*'''"''
Cooper: ''"The rocks were all covered in seagull shit. I'll never forget the sound it made when I took a knee. You know, the thing I-I can't figure out... is were you a monster back then? Or did you become one later?"''
({{FOTV|2|6}}) The two of them had a daughter, Janey, who was born on April 14, 2065.[[Cooper Howard]]: ''"You said you knew everything."''
Robert House: ''"I routinely design and run mathematical paradigms based on global, political, and socioeconomic conditions in an effort to... predict future events. And one spring morning, the data coalesced, and it told me, in no uncertain terms, that the world would... well, end."''
Cooper Howard: ''"Calculator told you that?"''
Robert House: ''"The date of the end of the world may not interest you, Mr. Howard. But the date the data coalesced might. April 14th, 2065, at 5:17 a.m. Is that date of any interest to you?"''
Cooper Howard: ''"That's my daughter's birthday."''
Robert House: ''"Oh, that is vexingly curious, isn't it? More curious is that you were not meant to come to Vegas this weekend. Your wife Barbara was meant to come alone. The moment that you bought your ticket to Las Vegas, the date the world was going to end... jumped forward by one month."''
Cooper Howard: ''"What are you, a f-fortune teller now?"''
Robert House: ''"I am a mathematician, a roboticist, and a casino owner. And I don't know yet how you figure into all of this, but you most certainly do. And I don't like unknown variables. Irksome. Not knowing exactly how you play a part in ending the world."''
({{FOTV|2|5}}) After the breakout of the [[Sino-American War]] and the [[China|Chinese]] invasion of [[Alaska]], Barb stayed home with their daughter while her husband was deployed to Alaska with the [[United States Marine Corps]]. She claims to Cooper that she was worried every day whether or not he would return alive; dreading every time she opened a letter in the mail, and she would always try to be near the phone in case she got a call saying he had been killed in action.[[The Ghoul|Cooper Howard]]: ''"No, I want to know about my freedom. I didn't go to war defending that freedom so that I could live in a cellar under the boot heel of Chairman Bud Askins."''
Barb Howard: ''"And while you were away at war, I stayed home."''
Cooper: ''"I know--"''
Barb: ''"I was checking the mail every day."''
Cooper: ''"I know."''
Barb: ''"I was waiting by the phone every night. And every night I was driving myself crazy imagining the worst. So, no, you do not need to tell me how bad war is, Coop."''
({{FOTV|1|6}}) ===Working for Vault-Tec=== At some point, Barb acquired a job for the [[Vault-Tec Corporation]] and, by the 2070s, had managed to climb the corporate ladder to a high-ranking executive position. She claimed to Cooper (and to herself) that all of her work at Vault-Tec was for the purpose of ensuring that her family would be guaranteed a future, whether that be in future employment or in survival after the bombs dropped.Barb Howard: ''"Every day I go into work and I think about how humanity can survive a nuclear event that will wipe out 90% of life on earth and I come home and you're talking to me about hiding out at a ranch up in Bakersfield. You know, I don't even know what planet you're on sometimes, Coop. But when the bombs drop, a two-hour drive ain't gonna cut it. So yes, there will be no dogs in the vaults. And no, none of it is ideal. But if billions of people are going to lose their lives, I will do whatever it takes to make sure the people I love... that is you and that is Janey... aren't among them. I have worked hard to make sure we go into a special vault for management, where we will oversee all of the other vaults. You don't get it. That is the best we can possibly hope for. For Janey."''
({{FOTV|1|6}})Barb Howard: ''"Don't walk away from me, Coop. I know more than you know, okay? There are over 12,000 nuclear warheads set-"''
[[Cooper Howard]]: ''"I'm not a board member. I am your husband."''
Barb: ''"Don't--"''
Cooper: ''"I don't care about your fuckin' statistics."''
Barb: ''"Statistics? This is about Janey."''
Cooper: ''"So... four our daughter, you would kill millions of people."''
Barb: ''"Don't do that."''
Cooper: ''"Billions of people. Other-other mothers just like you."''
Barb: ''"Don't do that, Coop, do not do that."''
Cooper: ''"Other daughters just like our daughter!"''
Barb: ''"Wouldn't you? For Janey. Wouldn't you? There are worse people out there than me, Coop."''
Cooper: ''"Who? Who could possibly be worse than you?"''
({{FOTV|2|6}}) On the former side, Barb managed to secure a role for Cooper in advertising Vault-Tec and its products, and also (only half-jokingly) considered having Janey join Vault-Tec's payroll as well in the future.[[Cooper Howard]]: ''"You ever... think about working somewhere else?"''
Barb Howard: ''"I used to. But with you doing these ads, it's... it's practically the family business. Maybe we get Janey a job in payroll when she's 15."''
({{FOTV|1|6}}) In the latter, Barb worked to land spots for herself and her family in a special Vault reserved for [[Vault-Tec Corporation|Vault-Tec]] management to oversee all the other Vaults—one of the "good Vaults," in her words.[[Cooper Howard]]: ''"Bud Askins."''
Barb Howard: ''"Bud Askins. Trust me, I know. The company's filled with guys like him. But Vault-Tec exists with or without me. Doesn't do anyone any good to complain from the sidelines."''
Cooper: ''"All I'm saying is we have this one life. Do you really want to spend your nine-to-fives working with these assholes?"''
Barb: ''"I need this job, Coop. It guarantees us a spot in the vaults."''
Cooper: ''"We got money. We can buy a spot in the vaults."''
Barb: ''"One of the good vaults."''
Cooper: ''"What's that supposed to mean?"''
Barb: ''"I'm doing what I can, okay? Just... trust me. Please."''
({{FOTV|1|6}}) This was especially important to Barb, as she was all too familiar with the corporate callousness of Vault-Tec managers such as her subordinate [[Bud Askins]],[[Bud Askins]] to Barb: ''"Our internal early alert system gives us at minimum 30 minutes from notice to ignition in downtown Los Angeles. You know, we'd be crazy not to offer specialized freeway lanes for our premium customers. I mean, that's just money on the table right there."''
({{FOTV|2|6}})[[Norm MacLean]]: ''"You don't strike me as the kind of person who would sign up for a program like this. Did you know going in about the Future Enterprise Ventures?"''
[[Claudia (TV series)|Claudia]]: ''"Like I said, I just started this job a week ago. But everything these people talked about sounded pretty nutty to me."''
Norm MacLean: ''"But you don't remember what they said? Nothing about doing something to the people in Vault 32 or 33?"''
Claudia: ''"No. There was this exec. Bud's boss? Her name was Barbara Howard. She was in charge of all the Vault proposals."''
({{FOTV|2|5}}) and she was also aware of the true purpose of the Vaults: Barb had the position of approving any and all proposals made for Vault experiments, and so had access to information about subjects such as the [[Forced Evolutionary Virus]]. She was also given notice of deadly flaws such as the high failure rate of the [[Water chip (TV series)|water chips]]. In effect, she had some ability to control who lived and who died.[[Vault-Tec engineer]] to Barb: ''"The bad news is our water chips have a 30% fail rate. The good news is we'll know which ones fail before installation. So, we get to choose who runs out of water. Any, uh, preferences?"''
({{FOTV|2|6}}) To her family, she heavily downplayed her role in Vault-Tec, presenting herself as a voice of reason among corporate zealots such as Bud Askins. These secrets weighed on Barb, but she ultimately chose not to resist, convincing herself it was all for her family's survival. She was further convinced not to defy the company when she received a threat from an [[Siggi Wilzig|unknown man]] representing [[Enclave|some unknown party]], warning that her family would be killed if she did not claim during an upcoming meeting of corporate leaders that Vault-Tec would be willing to guarantee the effectiveness of its Vaults by starting the nuclear war themselves. This convinced Barb that Vault-Tec was being controlled by a hidden power from the shadows, with plans of their own for the company and beyond,[[Siggi Wilzig|Wilzig]]: ''"You're just a very replaceable part in this machine."''
Barb Howard: ''"I'm sorry, who are you?"''
Wilzig: ''"But if you forget your place in the company... you'll die. And so will your family. The same will happen to me if I don't communicate this message. We're all in the same boat. And not one of us can stop it. You know that. You wake up knowing it. The leaders of the most powerful corporations will be gathering here. And when they do... you tell them... the only way to guarantee results is--"''
Barb Howard: ''"By dropping the bomb ourselves."''
({{FOTV|2|6}}) but it also convinced her to keep in her lane, seeing any further actions as futile;[[Cooper Howard]]: ''"Who threatened you?"''
Barb Howard: ''"Please, Coop. You don't need to get involved in any of this."''
Cooper Howard: ''"Who controls Vault-Tec?"''
Barb Howard: ''"I don't know."''
Cooper Howard: ''"Well, let's find out."''
Barb Howard: ''"No, no, no, no, no. This is not one of your movies with a happy ending. There is nothing we can do. If there was, I would have done it. I tried to do it. This deal is going forward whether we like it or not. Please, look at me. I am your wife. You know me. You know me."''
Cooper Howard: ''"I don't. I don't know you, Barbara."''
({{FOTV|2|6}}) even dropping the bombs could be justified if it kept her family safe. ===Falling out with Cooper=== Cooper's participation in Vault-Tec gradually began to wear on him, and his and Barb's affiliations with the company eventually became a point of contention in their relationship. However, they seemed to be stable overall, even as Barb was left conflicted by the apocalyptic plans she had been roped in being a part of. What Barb did not know was that Cooper had also become aware of her secrets: Cooper had met [[Lee Moldaver|Kate Williams]], a scientist whose work on [[cold fusion]] was bought up by Barb's division in Vault-Tec to prevent the technology from threatening their business model,[[Cooper Howard]]: ''"How do you know my wife?"''
Miss Williams: ''"My research company was acquired by her division. We were developing this kind of technology that's... difficult to monetize. Cold fusion. Infinite energy. That's what I was on the verge of achieving when Vault-Tec swept in and bought up every company I'd ever worked for."''
({{FOTV|1|7}}) and Williams gave him the means to spy on his wife and learn the truth. Cooper took this opportunity at just the right time to hear Barb delivering the proposal to start nuclear war.As shown in {{FOTV|1|8}} Not long afterwards, Barb was scheduled to visit Las Vegas during a defense contractors' summit in order to present the cold fusion technology to magnate [[Robert House]], who had struck a deal with Vault-Tec to receive it in exchange for having given them his "[[Brain-computer interface chip|automated man]]" mind control chip technology; he did not tell her what he would use it for, only that she would find out "after the bombs drop."[[Robert House's double]]: ''"RobCo presents the automated man. Spent a lot of time trying to make my machines more lifelike, but, hey, works the other way around, too."''
Barb Howard: ''"Mr. House, Vault-Tec and RobCo have always had a special arrangement. You have multiple Vaults to do with as you wish. If this is the research you'd like to pursue in the Vaults, you--"''
Robert House's double: ''"You must have missed the telegram. You're paying me for this. In exchange, I get Cold Fusion to power my little project in Vegas."''
Barb: ''"And what project is that?"''
House's double: ''"Might be above your paygrade. You'll find out about it after the bombs drop, I guess."''
({{FOTV|2|6}}) Cooper went with her, having been convinced by Williams that House would instead be selling nuclear weapons to Vault-Tec in exchange for cold fusion, which would then enable them to start the nuclear war. However, House subsequently met with Cooper, revealing his true intentions for the technology and that he did not believe Barb, Vault-Tec, or any other corporation would start the war—but that some other, hidden player might instead.{{FOTV|2|5}} Left reeling from the news but not actually believing House, Cooper subsequently confronted Barb, revealing that he knew of her and Vault-Tec's secrets. They briefly experienced a major falling out, though Barb still helped Cooper retrieve the cold fusion diode from [[Hank MacLean]], Barb's personal assistant, who had come with them to act as the carrier, and the two of them repaired their bond by agreeing to try and subvert what they believed were Vault-Tec's plans to start the apocalypse.{{FOTV|2|6}} To do so, Cooper gave the diode to the [[Last President of the United States|U.S. president]], with Barb's full awareness;{{FOTV|2|7}} though the two believed they had managed to end the conspiracy for good, they were proven wrong when Cooper was arrested on the orders of the [[House Un-American Activities Committee]] soon afterwards (the president was a member of the [[Enclave]], the hidden power behind Vault-Tec). Having been warned by House of his impending arrest, Cooper ordered his wife to let him take the fall for Janey's sake rather than fighting it, telling Barb to deny any involvement in his activities.{{FOTV|2|8}} The events that directly followed are currently unknown. Regardless, by October 2077, Barb and Cooper were publicly believed to have gotten divorced.[[Frank (TV series)|Frank]]: ''"Why the hell is Cooper Howard working kids' birthday parties?"''
[[Bob Spencer]]: ''"What else? Alimony."''
({{FOTV|1|1}}) On October 23, the day of the Great War, Cooper was with their daughter Janey, performing at a birthday party in [[Hollywood Hills]]. The ensuing events are unclear; Cooper was evidently separated from Janey at some point and either knew or believed that she and Barb had managed to get to safety inside one of Vault-Tec's management Vaults, though he did not know if he was correct, or which facility they would have entered. ===Post-War events=== Barb and Janey indeed had [[cryonics|cryo-stasis]] chambers allotted for them inside the executive preservation wing of the [[Las Vegas management Vault]], but it is unknown if either of them ever used them. Barb is suggested to have entered the facility at one point, though the only evidence of this is a [[Colorado]] postcard placed in her cryo chamber seemingly as a message for her husband.As seen in {{FOTV|2|5}}, the Vault-Tec facility has cryonic chambers with Barb's and Janey's names on them, which are shown to be occupied. The episode also seems to show a human silhouette inside Barb's cryonic chamber, though it is later revealed to be empty in "[[The Strip]]." Not knowing this, Cooper spent the next two centuries traveling all across the post-War United States in search of his family. Though he found numerous other Vaults over the years, including some management Vaults, he never found his family there, or even any clues to where they could have gone.[[Lucy MacLean]]: ''"I'd ask why my dad ran into a den of giant monsters, but you'd probably just tell me to shut the fudge up."''
[[The Ghoul]]: ''"[sighs] Before the war, there was a plan... for a special Vault. A Vault for management. That's where my wife is. Where my daughter is, too."''
Lucy MacLean: ''"You never found it?"''
The Ghoul: ''"Oh no, I found one, in California. It was empty. Found another one in Oregon. It was empty, too. Turns out, there's more than a few special Vaults for management sprinkled across the Wasteland. All of 'em empty. But I've never found one in Vegas."''
Lucy MacLean: ''"So, you think if my dad's in there, maybe your wife and daughter are, too?"''
The Ghoul: ''"Uh-huh. And now, they're surrounded by these fuckin' things."''
({{FOTV|2|5}}) This seemed to change in 2296, when Cooper (now [[ghoul]]ified, and going by [[the Ghoul]]) tracked a still-surviving Hank MacLean to New Vegas, convinced that Hank would lead him to a Vault-Tec facility where Barb and Janey may have been preserved. This seemed to be confirmed by Hank when he threatened Cooper into abandoning his pursuit by claiming to hold his family hostage via the control of their cryonic chambers in the Las Vegas management Vault, though this was merely a bluff. With the help of a reactivated House, Cooper located Barb and Janey's cryo pods inside the Vault, but they were empty aside from the postcard, with the message "Colorado was a good idea," referencing something that Cooper had told his wife before he was arrested. Cooper took this as a sign that Barb and Janey were still alive and set out in the direction of Colorado to search for them. ==''Fallout'' TV series== ===Season 1=== ====[[The Head]]==== [[File:FOTV Barb Thomas episode 3.png|thumb|200px|Barb and Cooper]] Barb appears to Cooper after he is finished filming a movie scene. She tells him how much she enjoys lavender. She gives Cooper a Vault jumpsuit to advertise the Vaults and watches Cooper give a thumbs up. ====[[The Trap]]==== After Cooper is done filming a [[Vault 4]] ad, he kisses Barb, and she informs him about a wrap party at their house. [[File:FOTV Barb Thomas episode 6.png|thumb|left|In the hot tub]] While relaxing in their hot tub, she denies the idea of Cooper getting their family away from Vault-Tec and city life. She shows Cooper her [[Pip-Boy 3000 Mark V]] and claims she needs this job because it will ensure them a spot in a good Vault, and asks Cooper to trust her. While eating breakfast, Cooper and Barb debate a new rule stating that dogs will not be allowed in the Vaults. Cooper is ultimately worried about infringement of freedom. ====[[The Radio]]==== Barb comes inside to take her Pip-Boy. Although Cooper is initially reluctant, he decides to put Moldaver's listening device into Barb's Pip-Boy. ====[[The Beginning]]==== {{Quotation|text=A nuclear event would be a tragedy... but also an opportunity. Perhaps the greatest opportunity in history. Because when we are the only ones left, there will be no one left to fight. A true monopoly. [...] This is our chance to make war obsolete. Because in our current societal configuration, which took shape without intentional guidance, we have friction. We have conflict, and we have war. And war, well... War never changes.|source=Barb}} [[File:Vaultcountrymap.jpg|thumb|200px|At the Vault-Tec meeting]] Barb is dropped off by Cooper at the [[Vault-Tec headquarters (TV series)|Vault-Tec headquarters]] for work, entering alongside Bud Askins. Using the listening device, Cooper hears Barb having a meeting with [[Robert House]], [[Frederick Sinclair]], Bud Askins, [[Julia Masters]], and [[Leon Von Felden]]. Barb presents Vault-Tec's proposal to run [[Vault#True purpose|experiments]] on vault inhabitants, offering to give each of the companies represented by the meeting attendees several vaults to run their own experiments unchecked. In response to skepticism from House, Barb also suggests that Vault-Tec could drop the first nuke to guarantee results for their shareholders, horrifying Cooper. ===Season 2=== ====[[The Innovator]]==== On the day of the Vault-Tec meeting, after discovering Barb's involvement in Vault-Tec's plans, Cooper initially decides to flee Los Angeles with Janey and Roosevelt. However, he is convinced by Kate Williams to stay and join Barb on her upcoming trip to Las Vegas, where she will apparently meet Robert House to deliver the [[cold fusion]] technology to him in exchange for receiving the nuclear weapons that Vault-Tec will use to kickstart nuclear war. Barb soon returns home, and is seen collecting herself at the front door before heading further inside to face her family. She then walks into the kitchen and is greeted by Cooper, who also had to compose himself before welcoming his wife home. ====[[The Profligate]]==== Cooper hears Barb quietly sniffling and sobbing in their kitchen, where he finds her attempting to put items into a "Keepsake" capsule for when they have to go into a Vault. Despite his unease over Barb's involvement with Vault-Tec's secret plans, Cooper still tries to comfort his wife, remarking that there may not be a need to go into a Vault. He changes the subject and says he has to go to an event with his friend Charles Whiteknife; as soon as he is out of sight, Cooper turns back in thought, conflicted between his love for Barb and knowing who she really is. ====[[The Wrangler]]==== Cooper and Barb prepare for their flight at [[Los Angeles International Airport]], where they are met in the terminal by her assistant [[Hank MacLean]]. After Cooper points out the locked briefcase handcuffed to Hank's wrist, Barb sends Hank ahead. She waits nearby after Cooper excuses himself to use a payphone, in truth to have a final meeting with Kate Williams where he says he will recover the cold fusion diode without killing House. Upon landing in Las Vegas, Barb and Cooper are driven in a limousine to the [[Lucky 38]], where they observe anti-war and anti-corporate protesters outside. [[Diane Welch|Congresswoman Welch]] is dragged out of the Lucky 38 by MPs after protesting inside. She is thrown onto the steps of the casino, and Cooper helps her up, telling her to keep at it, after which Barb gets him to follow her into the casino. Inside, Barb excuses herself to go speak with RobCo reps while Cooper offers to get them some drinks. In truth, he begins following Hank to try and get at his briefcase, but is pulled away when Robert House himself summons him to the [[Lucky 38 penthouse]] for a private meeting via his [[Robert House's double|body double]]. During his meeting with House, Cooper is told the CEO's belief that it will not be Barb or anyone at the corporate meeting who will drop the bombs. However, he does believe that Barb and Cooper are more involved than originally thought. He reveals that he has been running mathematical equations according to various factors, all in an effort to predict the end of the world, and achieved the first conclusive results on the same day that Barb gave birth to their daughter Janey; this indicated to House that the Howard family would have an important role to play in future events. House adds that Cooper's decision to travel to Vegas with his wife in the present also had an influence, shortening the calculated timeframe of the war's start by a month, which further cemented this belief. Cooper leaves his meeting with House in emotional turmoil and tries to drown out his thoughts with alcohol, causing him to go on an alcoholic bender and make a spectacle of himself on the casino floor until Barb finds him and brings him to recover in their hotel room. As she nurses her hungover husband in their hotel room, Cooper wakes up and tells her they need to talk. ====[[The Other Player]]==== In a flashback set before the Vault-Tec meeting in "The Beginning," Barb is shown at work fielding several staff meetings, including a promotional campaign explicitly depicting nuclear explosions in Los Angeles; an R&D meeting with an [[Vault-Tec engineer|engineer]] who reveals that the Vaults' [[water chip]]s have a 30% fail rate that upper management wants to purposefully exploit; and a proposal by [[Bud Askins]] to create specialized freeway lanes for premium Vault-Tec customers. Another meeting is with Robert House (actually the double), wherein Barb learns that RobCo is licensing their [[brain-computer interface chip]] technology to Vault-Tec; in exchange, House is being given ownership of the [[Cold fusion|cold fusion diode]] for his own uses, a fact Barb was not privy to. She tries to ask what his plans are, but House slyly points out she will have to wait for the bombs to fall to find out. The meetings leave Barb increasingly uncomfortable and eventually bring her to tears at the thought of Vault-Tec's plans. Back to the relative present in the Lucky 38, Cooper starts their talk by reminiscing about the day he proposed to Barb at Catalina before revealing he knows about the plans she made with the corporate leaders at the Vault-Tec conference, stunning her silent. Barb tries to convince him of her side, but he denounces her complicity in a plan that would kill millions if not billions, including families just like theirs. However, Barb shoots back that Cooper would do the same if it meant protecting their daughter, to which Cooper does not respond. Barb tries to emphasize that there are people involved who are worse than her, but Cooper insults her belief that anyone could be worse than her in their situation, leaving Barb distraught. The scene returns to the Vault-Tec headquarters, right after Barb's meeting with Robert House's double. After House leaves, Barb tries to get her assistant [[Betty Pearson]] to find out everything she can about the cold fusion technology, and responds to Betty's concerns with a remark that none of what Vault-Tec is doing with House is a good idea. As she enters an elevator, she finds herself in an impromptu meeting with [[Siggi Wilzig]], whom she does not recognize. He informs her that any actions she takes against "the company" to stop the coming events will result in deadly consequences for her family, then gives her the exact words she would later use at the boardroom meeting where she advocated for Vault-Tec to directly instigate the apocalypse. Back in the Lucky 38 again, Barb has evidently told Cooper about her encounter with the mysterious man and what Cooper heard while spying on the meeting. Cooper still is convinced that they can do something to avert the plans to end the world, but Barb pleads with him not to, believing that there is nothing left they can do, and claiming that she had tried all of the options she had, which all failed. Cooper remains undeterred and leaves to do "something." That turns out to be getting Hank MacLean drunk. After bringing him back to their hotel room, Cooper pours a drink for them both, drugging Hank's drink with Barb's sleeping pills to break into the briefcase. Cooper discovers it is an extractor gun but is confused about what it is. When Barb returns to the room, she finds Cooper holding the extractor gun. She wordlessly takes it and removes the cold fusion diode implanted inside Hank's neck via the gun. She shows it to Cooper as he starts to understand more about what his wife has had to go through. ====[[The Handoff]]==== In their hotel room in the Lucky 38, after having acquired the cold fusion diode, Barb hides as Cooper arranges for a maid ([[Steph Harper]]) to take the passed-out Hank away to his own room. Barb reemerges after Steph leaves, and she shares a look with her husband. Later, Cooper meets with Representative Welch to try and negotiate a way to deliver the cold fusion diode to the government, though he purposefully omits his wife's agreement with his plans. He agrees to Welch's offer to arrange a meeting with the [[Last President of the United States|U.S. president]], to whom Cooper can personally hand the diode. Barb evidently also agrees with this, as she later accompanies Cooper on the streets of Las Vegas to the assigned meeting place, though she stays away as Cooper delivers the diode to the president. ====[[The Strip]]==== In a flashback at [[Camp McCarran|McCarran International Airport]], Cooper and Barb share drinks, satisfied at having seemingly averted Vault-Tec's conspiracy. They briefly discuss their next plans, with Barb now agreeing with Cooper's suggestion to go to Bakersfield and Cooper now suggesting Colorado instead. The two learn that Hank and Steph have gotten engaged before House calls Cooper with a warning that something is about to happen and a reminder that House had told Cooper that there are worse people than him in the world. Seeing [[U.S. federal agent|several men]] approaching and deducing that he is about to be arrested, Cooper orders Barb to let him take the fall for what happened while she denies any knowledge of it so as to protect Janey. After they kiss one final time, Barb tearfully watches as the men, federal agents, arrest her husband on the authority of the [[House Un-American Activities Committee]]. In the present, House's [[Artificial personality|AI backup]] helps the Ghoul find Barb and Janey's cryo pods in the [[Las Vegas management Vault]]. However, when House opens them, they are both empty. On the seat of Barb's pod is a Colorado postcard with a message reading "Colorado was a good idea," seemingly from Barb herself, referencing her husband's idea that they go there before he was arrested. With relief, the Ghoul tells House that for the first time in 200 years, he has a clue that his family may still be alive. The Ghoul heads for Colorado with [[CX404|Dogmeat]] in search of his wife and daughter. ==Personality== The initial interactions between Cooper and his wife show them both to be deeply in love with each other, to the extent that Cooper willingly starts a collaborative media campaign as Vault-Tec's spokesman solely for the sake of making Barb happy. However, Barb's dedication to working her way up the corporate ladder of Vault-Tec to get her family into a "good" Vault, and the compromises in personal freedoms he observes coming with that, strains Cooper's marriage to Barb. Once he is helped by Kate Williams to see that there are deeper, darker secrets to Barb and Vault-Tec, Cooper's trust in her fractures, ultimately breaking apart once he discovers via spying on her meeting with the corporate leaders that Barb planned to set the nuclear apocalypse in motion to keep Vault-Tec and its allies in power regardless of the immense death toll. However, it is only after finally having an honest talk with Barb and confronting her with what he overheard that Cooper discovers that what he originally thought was Barb's willingness to condemn humanity to its destruction was masking a great inner turmoil; Barb was not willingly making plans to start a nuclear war, but she felt she could not save her family from the threat posed by those holding her in their power, and was forced to cooperate, hoping that all of them could live through the end of the world together. Even once husband and wife finally understand all of this, Barb is desperate to stop Cooper from continuing in his plan to oppose the conspiracy and its creators, as she knows there is little, if anything, either of them can do against entities with far too much power and influence to be stopped. ==Notable quotes== * {{Inline quote|I'm doing what I can, okay?
